parsed.explanation: Combined regime is high risk. Parent-nation border screening treats sex-document doubt as grounds for refusal and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, and trans athletes are barred; immigration and custody records document severe abuse. Federal facilities exclude trans people by birth sex, while this division currently has no state bathroom ban or criminalisation but a pending bill and narrowing ID law. State hate-crime and accommodation protections are absent; local ordinances cover only part of the population. Minors face care bans. Courts and legal aid provide partial, uncertain mitigation. There is no execution or general imprisonment for trans identity, but outing at the border or in custody carries severe consequences.

entry_documents.exposure: National screening cable directs refusal where documents or records cast doubt on sex; suspected misrepresentation can support lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans-athlete entry ban; foreign X markers may be questioned; neighbouring citizens detained over visa issues.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; fraud finding is not automatic and requires four elements; passport rules are under litigation; legal-aid FAQ exists.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch at border triggers secondary review and possible refusal or stranding; detention can follow visa or document escalation.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse. National corrections adopted conversion-therapy-like policies and denial of care; state prison funds are barred for transition care.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented working custody protection; national hate-crime statute does not govern custody conditions.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Border fraud suspicion or immigration violation can move a traveller into custody where harm is documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity; many divisions ban such use; this division's 2025 bathroom bill is pending but not enacted, and no current state statute bars or criminalises facility use.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 2017 repeal; no state statute barring facility use; local ordinances cover roughly 30% of population.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facilities create universal exposure; state facilities are currently open but legislative risk remains.

care_services.exposure: State bans gender-affirming care for minors and bars state funds for transition care in prison; national proposed insurance bar under 18; hospital visitation is only through designated-visitor rules.
care_services.protection: Adult emergency-care denial is not documented; hospital visitation statute exists.
care_services.interaction: A minor traveller cannot obtain care in state; adult care funding or insurance may be limited; custody care is denied.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups for priority neutralisation; justice reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; school investigation executive order; official hostility.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy says it will not target simple disagreement; courts enjoined some orders; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises scrutiny for visible activists; ordinary tourists are less directly targeted but the climate is hostile.

minors_guardians.exposure: State bans puberty blockers, hormones and surgery under 18; national executive order frames minor care as mutilation and directs school investigations; parental-notification law.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care denial in state and possible school or medical scrutiny; border arrest is not documented.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime statute excludes gender identity and sexual orientation; statewide accommodation protections are absent; local ordinances cover roughly 30% of population; opinion majorities support birth-sex documents and sports bans.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; local ordinances exist in the largest city and one county.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: An assault may not be charged as a state bias crime; federal recourse is possible; no documented visitor violence pattern is established.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport policy is in effect; legal challenges are unresolved; the 2025 bathroom bill could return; county application of the birth-certificate original-sex display is unknown.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts enjoined some orders; civil-liberties suit exists; legal-aid FAQ exists; national hate-crime coverage exists.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Protection is a patchwork by locality and litigation status; a visitor must verify current rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar port denial after document mismatch, with invasive review and no detention. This dossier adds national screening refusal and lifetime fraud exposure, documented custody abuse, and federal facility exclusion, so it is somewhat lower (less safe), though it lacks general criminalisation of trans identity.

The anchor has entry denial without detention and a functioning ombudsman or legal aid. This dossier documents harsher national entry screening, custody abuse and facility restrictions, placing it below 0.35-A.

The anchor involves service refusal but a working non-discrimination code and no detention. This dossier has state-imposed entry and facility exposures, custody harm and limited state recourse, clearly below 0.55-B.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is a patchwork: national border, document, facility and custody policies supply the hardest exposures, while the division adds restrictive ID and minor-care laws but currently no facility criminalisation. A traveller may pass ordinary tourist interactions, but an outed document mismatch can strand them, trigger fraud findings, or lead to custody with documented abuse. State bias-crime and accommodation recourse is thin; federal hate-crime law and litigation are partial protections. The pending 2025 bathroom bill and unresolved court challenges make the present picture unstable.
